facts.claim: Sennrich and colleagues (2016) brought byte pair encoding to neural translation: rare and unknown words are encoded as sequences of subword units.
GPT-2 (Radford and colleagues, 2019) runs BPE on bytes, not characters: a base vocabulary of only 256, so it can encode any Unicode string.
OpenAI's rule of thumb for English: 1 token is about 4 characters, and 100 tokens about 75 words.
Anthropic: usage and billing reflect the model's own tokenizer's counts, so count prompts with the model you plan to use.
Anthropic: Claude Opus 4.7 and later Claude models use a newer tokenizer; the same text gives roughly 30% more tokens than on earlier Claude models, depending on the content.
In October 2026, Anthropic listed Claude Sonnet 5.5's base input price at $2 per million tokens; prices change.
Anthropic's token counting endpoint returns an estimate: the tokens actually used can differ by a small amount.
Petrov and colleagues (2023): the same text translated into different languages can take up to 15 times as many tokens.
Petrov and colleagues (2023): even character- and byte-level models show over 4 times the difference in length for some language pairs.
OpenAI: an embedding is a list of numbers, and the distance between two embeddings measures how related their texts are.
OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small gives 1,536 numbers per text by default; text-embedding-3-large gives 3,072.
OpenAI's embeddings have length 1, so cosine similarity can be computed with just a dot product; OpenAI recommends cosine similarity.
RAG's embedding model, all-MiniLM-L6-v2, maps a sentence or paragraph to 384 numbers and reads its input as word pieces (WordPiece), not BPE tokens.
